item.title: Write a Correction to an Overconfident Forecast
item.prompt_text: Your team told residents that a hall would probably reopen in May. The date assumed one supplier could deliver everything together. The supplier now offers two deliveries, and the team knows the earliest possible opening has moved to June, but the exact date remains uncertain. Write a correction that takes responsibility for the earlier impression, explains what the team can now say, and sets a transparent rule for the next update.
item.audience: people following a community hall improvement project
item.target_grammar: Calibrated certainty, acknowledgement and conditional public commitments.
item.target_structure: Summarise the correction up front, explain why the forecast changed, and commit to a specific trigger for releasing new information.

checklist.point: Acknowledge the earlier impression and own its limits.
Explain what changed with the supplier.
Distinguish the earliest date from a confirmed one.
Give a clear rule for future updates.
